last_outcome: M1-16 (iteration 28): assembled the flight screen -- FlightScreen.tsx composes full-bleed FlightMap, a title and FlightCard with a live bird marker positioned by M1-15's projectPoint, driven by flightStateAt(flight, now()). FlightMap gained an optional markerPoint prop rendering an SVG <Circle>. The marker updates on a requestAnimationFrame loop by default, throttled to FlightCard's own 1 Hz setInterval tick when reducedMotion is true; both share one tick() helper that reports arrival and stops rescheduling itself once now() >= arrivesAtMs. The initial nowMs is lazily computed from now() at mount, so a flight mounted after arrival renders at rest at the destination on the first frame with no replay. Self-review found two real issues beyond the two listed acceptance criteria: arcSegments/projectSegments were recomputed every single frame despite never changing for a mounted flight (fixed with useMemo keyed on origin/destination/viewport), and neither the frame loop nor the reduced-motion interval ever stopped after arrival (fixed via the shared tick() return value, regression-tested by asserting the live timer count drops by exactly one after arrival). Also fixed: the test file's own hand-copied PADDING_RATIO literal risked drifting from the component's -- now exported and imported instead. Added a flight-demo.tsx route (honest placeholder, no real send/receive flow exists yet -- M1-07/M1-08 still todo, no server-time-sync mechanism built) and a flight-screen dev story with its own byte-identical screenshot pair. pnpm run verify green: gate:roadmap ok, 25 done/7 pending; gate:tests floor raised 187 -> 193 (+6: 5 FlightScreen tests + 1 new shot.test.ts story pair test).
